newsitem.title: USA: Florida identifies patients in smoking suit.
newsitem.headline: Florida identifies patients in smoking suit.

text.p: The state of Florida said Tuesday that it had identified 860,000 Medicaid patients who received "taxpayer-sponsored" treatment for smoking-related illnesses during fiscal year 1994-95 and fiscal year 1995-96.
Florida said it had delivered more than 40 boxes containing 215,000 pages of Medicaid records to the Palm Beach County trial court to comply with a judge's order.
Florida is suing the tobacco industry to recover what it says are billions of dollars in taxpayer money spent to treat Medicaid patients suffering from tobacco-related illnesses.
Companies sued include Philip Morris Cos Inc and B.A.T Industries Plc, among others.
Florida said its delivery of the documents kept the case on track for trial on August 4, 1997 and fully complies with Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen's Sept. 16 order.
"Today, we're taking another giant step forward in our fight to bring tobacco justice to our taxpayers and children," Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles said in a statement.

The Medicaid records delivered to the court included an identification number for each Medicaid patient, the name of each health care provider, the date of the patient's death, the procedure code for services provided and the summary cost in dollars for the medical care provided.
Florida sued the tobacco industry under a controversial 1994 state law that stripped cigarette makers of most of their traditional defenses in a liability lawsuit.

Tobacco stocks had jumped in September after the news that the judge had dismissed pre-1994 claims in Florida's lawsuit in the same ruling in which he required the state to provide documentation on all of the cases.
Florida officials had responded that Cohen's ruling had left the most important parts of the lawsuit intact.
